content.text:
Complete the offline CPU sharing-replay project in `/workspace/submission`.
Read `PROTOCOL.md` for the complete event, objective and certificate contract.
Read `MODULES.md` for the provided multi-file code and repair sites.
Use the CPU project as your starting point; internals may be replaced.
Replay cumulative topology/traffic changes and immutable worker proposals.
Handle delayed, duplicate, superseded and obsolete deliveries explicitly.
Advance the cached coordinator only when its partial barrier permits progress.
Certify worker allocations and the controller projection in their different units.
Preserve checkpoint state, generation boundaries and scaled duals on retuning.
Report every owned unroutable commodity for an infeasible route proposal.
Validate the entire request before replay, including operations after restores.
Every illegal input and its exact error response are defined in the protocol.
The entry point is `python3 submission/main.py`, reading one JSON value to EOF.
Python3.11.14 and offline NumPy1.26.4 are provisioned; no network is needed.
Run `python3 check.py submission` for the small public sanity check.
For direct development, run `python3 bootstrap.py` and use the documented
PYTHONPATH command. Fix or replace any project files; auxiliary files are allowed.
Submit the entire `submission/` tree with its root `main.py`.
All numeric limits, file bounds and process restrictions are in `PROTOCOL.md`.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
